source.text: Μετὰ τοῦτο εἶδον τέσσαρας ἀγγέλους ἑστῶτας ἐπὶ τὰς τέσσαρας γωνίας τῆς γῆς, κρατοῦντας τοὺς τέσσαρας ἀνέμους τῆς γῆς, ἵνα μὴ πνέῃ ἄνεμος ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς μήτε ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης μήτε ἐπὶ πᾶν δένδρον.

records.literal_gloss: After this I saw four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth, so that not would blow wind on the earth nor on the sea nor on any tree.

en.L: After this I saw four angels standing at the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth, so that no wind would blow on the earth or on the sea or on any tree.
en.B: Next I saw four angels standing at the four corners of the earth. They were holding back the earth's four winds, so that no wind could blow on land or sea or on any tree.
en.R: After this I saw four angels. They were standing at the four corners of the earth. They were holding back the four winds so that no wind would blow on the land, on the sea, or on any tree.

decisions.choice: the four corners and the four winds: the whole earth, and the judgments held back
decisions.reason: "The four corners of the earth" means the whole earth (Isaiah 11:12; Ezekiel 7:2). In the prophets the four winds bring God's judgment (Jeremiah 49:36; Daniel 7:2), and Zechariah 6:5 calls the four chariots with their horses "the four winds of heaven", which ties them to the horsemen of chapter 6. Here the winds are held back.

decisions.choice: a pause before the seventh seal
decisions.reason: Chapter 6 ended with the question "Who is able to stand?" (6:17). Before the seventh seal is opened (8:1), chapter 7 answers it: God's people are sealed, and a great crowd stands before the throne.

source.text: καὶ εἶδον ἄλλον ἄγγελον ἀναβαίνοντα ἀπὸ ἀνατολῆς ἡλίου, ἔχοντα σφραγῖδα θεοῦ ζῶντος, καὶ ἔκραξεν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ τοῖς τέσσαρσιν ἀγγέλοις οἷς ἐδόθη αὐτοῖς ἀδικῆσαι τὴν γῆν καὶ τὴν θάλασσαν, λέγων· Μὴ ἀδικήσητε τὴν γῆν μήτε τὴν θάλασσαν μήτε τὰ δένδρα, ἄχρι σφραγίσωμεν τοὺς δούλους τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν ἐπὶ τῶν μετώπων αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And I saw another angel ascending from rising of sun, having seal of God living, and he cried out with voice loud to the four angels to whom it was given to them to harm the earth and the sea, \v 3 saying: Not harm the earth nor the sea nor the trees until we seal the slaves of the God of us on the foreheads of them.

en.L: And I saw another angel coming up from the rising of the sun, having the seal of the living God, and he cried out with a loud voice to the four angels to whom it had been given to harm the earth and the sea, \v 3 saying, "Do not harm the earth or the sea or the trees until we have sealed the slaves of our God on their foreheads."
en.B: I saw yet another angel, coming up from where the sun rises and carrying the seal of the living God. In a loud voice he called to the four angels who had been allowed to harm the earth and the sea: \v 3 "Hold off from harming the earth, the sea, and the trees until we have marked the servants of our God with a seal on their foreheads."
en.R: Then I saw another angel coming from the east. He had the seal of the living God. He shouted to the four angels who had been given power to hurt the land and the sea. \v 3 He said, "Wait! Do not hurt the land or the sea or the trees until we have put God's mark on the foreheads of the servants of our God."

decisions.choice: a seal: a mark of ownership and protection
decisions.reason: A seal pressed into wax or clay showed who owned something and kept it safe. In Ezekiel 9:4-6 a mark is put on the foreheads of those who grieve over Jerusalem's sins, and they are spared when judgment falls. God's people are sealed before the winds are released; later, those who follow the beast bear its mark on the forehead or hand (13:16-17; 14:1).

decisions.choice: from the rising of the sun: from the east
decisions.reason: The east is where the sun rises, and in Ezekiel 43:2 the glory of God comes from the east. The angel comes from the direction of light and blessing.

decisions.choice: the slaves of our God
decisions.reason: See the note on 1:1.

decisions.choice: from the rising of the sun (L); from where the sun rises (B); from the east (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek phrase; Balanced keeps the picture; Readable gives the direction.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m3) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

source.text: Καὶ ἤκουσα τὸν ἀριθμὸν τῶν ἐσφραγισμένων, ἑκατὸν τεσσεράκοντα τέσσαρες χιλιάδες, ἐσφραγισμένοι ἐκ πάσης φυλῆς υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ·

records.literal_gloss: And I heard the number of those having been sealed, 144,000, having been sealed out of every tribe of sons of Israel:

en.L: And I heard the number of those who were sealed, 144,000, sealed from every tribe of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.
en.B: And I heard how many were sealed: 144,000, sealed from every tribe of the Israelites.
en.R: Then I heard how many people were sealed. There were 144,000. They came from all the tribes of Israel.

decisions.choice: 144,000 from the tribes of Israel: the complete people of God
alternatives: Jewish believers only, as distinct from the great crowd of 7:9
a literal number of people from the twelve tribes
decisions.reason: The number is twelve times twelve times a thousand: the full number of God's people, counted like an army by tribes (compare Numbers 1). John hears the number and then sees a crowd no one can count (7:9), as he heard of a Lion and saw a Lamb (5:5-6). Many therefore take the 144,000 and the great crowd as the same people seen in two ways: God's people as the true Israel (compare Galatians 6:16; James 1:1). Others take them as Jewish believers sealed for protection, or as a literal number. The text does not say outright.

decisions.choice: children of Israel (L); the Israelites (B); Israel (R)
decisions.reason: As in 2:14.

source.text: ἐκ φυλῆς Ἰούδα δώδεκα χιλιάδες ἐσφραγισμένοι, ἐκ φυλῆς Ῥουβὴν δώδεκα χιλιάδες, ἐκ φυλῆς Γὰδ δώδεκα χιλιάδες, ἐκ φυλῆς Ἀσὴρ δώδεκα χιλιάδες, ἐκ φυλῆς Νεφθαλὶμ δώδεκα χιλιάδες, ἐκ φυλῆς Μανασσῆ δώδεκα χιλιάδες, ἐκ φυλῆς Συμεὼν δώδεκα χιλιάδες, ἐκ φυλῆς Λευὶ δώδεκα χιλιάδες, ἐκ φυλῆς Ἰσσαχὰρ δώδεκα χιλιάδες, ἐκ φυλῆς Ζαβουλὼν δώδεκα χιλιάδες, ἐκ φυλῆς Ἰωσὴφ δώδεκα χιλιάδες, ἐκ φυλῆς Βενιαμὶν δώδεκα χιλιάδες ἐσφραγισμένοι.

records.literal_gloss: Out of tribe of Judah 12,000 sealed, out of tribe of Reuben 12,000, out of tribe of Gad 12,000, \v 6 out of tribe of Asher 12,000, out of tribe of Naphtali 12,000, out of tribe of Manasseh 12,000, \v 7 out of tribe of Simeon 12,000, out of tribe of Levi 12,000, out of tribe of Issachar 12,000, \v 8 out of tribe of Zebulun 12,000, out of tribe of Joseph 12,000, out of tribe of Benjamin 12,000 sealed.

en.L: From the tribe of Judah 12,000 sealed, from the tribe of Reuben 12,000, from the tribe of Gad 12,000, \v 6 from the tribe of Asher 12,000, from the tribe of Naphtali 12,000, from the tribe of Manasseh 12,000, \v 7 from the tribe of Simeon 12,000, from the tribe of Levi 12,000, from the tribe of Issachar 12,000, \v 8 from the tribe of Zebulun 12,000, from the tribe of Joseph 12,000, from the tribe of Benjamin 12,000 sealed.
en.B: From the tribe of Judah, 12,000 were sealed; from the tribe of Reuben, 12,000; from the tribe of Gad, 12,000; \v 6 from the tribe of Asher, 12,000; from the tribe of Naphtali, 12,000; from the tribe of Manasseh, 12,000; \v 7 from the tribe of Simeon, 12,000; from the tribe of Levi, 12,000; from the tribe of Issachar, 12,000; \v 8 from the tribe of Zebulun, 12,000; from the tribe of Joseph, 12,000; and from the tribe of Benjamin, 12,000 were sealed.
en.R: There were 12,000 from the tribe of Judah, 12,000 from Reuben, 12,000 from Gad, \v 6 12,000 from Asher, 12,000 from Naphtali, 12,000 from Manasseh, \v 7 12,000 from Simeon, 12,000 from Levi, 12,000 from Issachar, \v 8 12,000 from Zebulun, 12,000 from Joseph, and 12,000 from Benjamin.

decisions.choice: an unusual list of the tribes: Judah first, Dan and Ephraim left out
decisions.reason: The Old Testament lists the twelve tribes in many orders, but none like this one. Judah, the tribe of the Messiah (5:5), comes first instead of Reuben, the firstborn. Dan is missing, and Ephraim is named only through Joseph, while Levi, usually left out of tribal lists, is included, as is Manasseh. Dan was linked with idolatry (Judges 18:30; 1 Kings 12:29-30), and Irenaeus, in the second century, mentioned a belief that the antichrist would come from Dan. The text gives no reason.

decisions.choice: the list shortened (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names "the tribe" once and lists the rest by name, so the list is easier to read aloud.

source.text: Μετὰ ταῦτα εἶδον, καὶ ἰδοὺ ὄχλος πολύς, ὃν ἀριθμῆσαι αὐτὸν οὐδεὶς ἐδύνατο, ἐκ παντὸς ἔθνους καὶ φυλῶν καὶ λαῶν καὶ γλωσσῶν, ἑστῶτες ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου καὶ ἐνώπιον τοῦ ἀρνίου, περιβεβλημένους στολὰς λευκάς, καὶ φοίνικες ἐν ταῖς χερσὶν αὐτῶν·

records.literal_gloss: After these things I saw, and behold a crowd great, which to number it no one was able, out of every nation and tribes and peoples and tongues, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, having been clothed with robes white, and palms in the hands of them;

en.L: After these things I looked, and look, a great crowd that no one was able to count, from every nation and [from all] tribes and peoples and languages, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, clothed in white robes, and palm branches in their hands.
en.B: After this I looked, and I saw a crowd so vast that no one could number it. They came from every nation and from all tribes and peoples and languages, and they stood before the throne and before the Lamb, dressed in white robes, with palm branches in their hands.
en.R: After this I looked, and I saw a huge crowd of people. There were so many that no one could count them. They came from every nation, tribe, people, and language. They were standing in front of the throne and in front of the Lamb. They wore white robes and held palm branches in their hands.

decisions.choice: a crowd no one could count: God's promise to Abraham
decisions.reason: God promised Abraham descendants as many as the stars and the sand, beyond counting (Genesis 15:5; 32:12). The promise is fulfilled in a crowd from every nation. The four-part phrase is the one used in 5:9.

decisions.choice: white robes and palm branches: victory and celebration
decisions.reason: White robes belong to those who overcome (3:5; 6:11). Palm branches were waved at festivals and victories, at the Feast of Tabernacles (Leviticus 23:40) and when Jesus entered Jerusalem (John 12:13).

decisions.choice: crowd
decisions.reason: ὄχλος is the ordinary word for a crowd; "multitude" is older English.

source.text: καὶ κράζουσι φωνῇ μεγάλῃ λέγοντες· Ἡ σωτηρία τῷ θεῷ ἡμῶν τῷ καθημένῳ ἐπὶ τῷ θρόνῳ καὶ τῷ ἀρνίῳ.

records.literal_gloss: And they cry out with voice loud saying: The salvation to the God of us the [one] sitting on the throne and to the Lamb.

en.L: And they cry out with a loud voice, saying, "Salvation [belongs] to our God, who is seated on the throne, and to the Lamb!"
en.B: With a loud voice they cry out: "To our God, seated on the throne, and to the Lamb, salvation belongs!"
en.R: They shouted, "Our God who sits on the throne has saved us, and so has the Lamb!"

decisions.choice: salvation belongs to God: he is the one who saves
decisions.reason: σωτηρία means deliverance, rescue or victory. To say that it belongs to God and the Lamb is to praise them as the ones who saved this crowd. Psalm 3:8 and Jonah 2:9 say, "Salvation belongs to the LORD."

decisions.choice: salvation (L, B); has saved us (R)
decisions.reason: Salvation is a key term. Readable uses the verb "saved", which the key-term list allows, to make the cry a plain sentence.

source.text: καὶ πάντες οἱ ἄγγελοι εἱστήκεισαν κύκλῳ τοῦ θρόνου καὶ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων καὶ τῶν τεσσάρων ζῴων, καὶ ἔπεσαν ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου ἐπὶ τὰ πρόσωπα αὐτῶν καὶ προσεκύνησαν τῷ θεῷ, λέγοντες· Ἀμήν· ἡ εὐλογία καὶ ἡ δόξα καὶ ἡ σοφία καὶ ἡ εὐχαριστία καὶ ἡ τιμὴ καὶ ἡ δύναμις καὶ ἡ ἰσχὺς τῷ θεῷ ἡμῶν εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων· ἀμήν.

records.literal_gloss: And all the angels were standing around the throne and the elders and the four living creatures, and they fell before the throne on the faces of them and worshiped the God, \v 12 saying: Amen, the blessing and the glory and the wisdom and the thanksgiving and the honor and the power and the strength to the God of us into the ages of the ages; amen.

en.L: And all the angels stood around the throne and the elders and the four living creatures, and they fell on their faces before the throne and worshiped God, \v 12 saying, "Amen! The blessing and the glory and the wisdom and the thanksgiving and the honor and the power and the might [be] to our God for the ages of the ages. Amen."
en.B: Every angel stood in a circle around the throne, the elders, and the four living creatures, and they threw themselves face down before the throne and worshiped God. \v 12 "Amen!" they said. "Blessing and glory, wisdom and thanksgiving, honor and power and might be to our God forever and ever! Amen."
en.R: All the angels were standing around the throne, the elders, and the four living creatures. They bowed down in front of the throne with their faces to the ground. They worshiped God. \v 12 They said, "Amen! Praise, glory, wisdom, thanks, honor, power, and strength belong to our God forever and ever! Amen!"

decisions.choice: seven words of praise, framed by Amen
decisions.reason: As in 5:12, seven words of praise under one article make a complete ascription. The angels begin with "Amen", agreeing with the crowd's cry (7:10), and end with it.

decisions.choice: blessing (L, B); praise (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:12.

source.text: Καὶ ἀπεκρίθη εἷς ἐκ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων λέγων μοι· Οὗτοι οἱ περιβεβλημένοι τὰς στολὰς τὰς λευκὰς τίνες εἰσὶν καὶ πόθεν ἦλθον;

records.literal_gloss: And answered one of the elders saying to me: These the [ones] having been clothed with the robes the white, who are they and from where did they come?

en.L: And one of the elders answered, saying to me, "These who are clothed in the white robes, who are they, and from where have they come?"
en.B: One of the elders turned to me with a question: "Those clothed in the white robes, who are they, and from where have they come?"
en.R: Then one of the elders asked me, "Who are these people dressed in white robes? Where did they come from?"

decisions.choice: answered: began to speak
decisions.reason: ἀπεκρίθη "answered" is a Hebrew way of saying that someone spoke up, even when no question has been asked.

decisions.choice: a teacher's question
decisions.reason: The elder asks in order to explain, as the angel does in Zechariah 4:2-5 and 4:11-14.

source.text: καὶ εἴρηκα αὐτῷ· Κύριέ μου, σὺ οἶδας.

records.literal_gloss: And I have said to him: Lord of me, you know.

en.L: And I said to him, "My lord, you know."
en.B: I answered, "Sir, you are the one who knows."

decisions.choice: my lord: a respectful address, not a title of God
decisions.reason: Κύριέ is the ordinary polite way of addressing a superior, "sir". John is speaking to one of the elders. The answer echoes Ezekiel's reply to God, "O Lord GOD, you know" (Ezekiel 37:3).

decisions.choice: my lord (L); Sir (B, R)
decisions.reason: Lowercase "lord" or "sir" shows that this is respect for the elder, not a prayer to God (m1).

source.text: καὶ εἶπέν μοι· Οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ ἐρχόμενοι ἐκ τῆς θλίψεως τῆς μεγάλης, καὶ ἔπλυναν τὰς στολὰς αὐτῶν καὶ ἐλεύκαναν αὐτὰς ἐν τῷ αἵματι τοῦ ἀρνίου.

records.literal_gloss: And he said to me: These are the [ones] coming out of the tribulation the great, and they washed the robes of them and made white them in the blood of the Lamb.

en.L: And he said to me, "These are the ones coming out of the great affliction, and they have washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.
en.B: He said to me, "These are the ones who are coming out of the great affliction. They have washed their robes in the blood of the Lamb and made them white.
en.R: He said, "These are the people who have come through the time of terrible suffering. They have washed their robes in the blood of the Lamb and made them white.

decisions.choice: the great affliction: the time of suffering for God's people
alternatives: only a final period of distress just before the end
the whole suffering of the church in every age
decisions.reason: Daniel 12:1 speaks of a time of distress such as never was, and Jesus spoke of great distress (Matthew 24:21). ἐρχόμενοι is present, "those who are coming out", which may mean that they are still arriving. Whether the great affliction is a final period or the suffering that runs through the church's life (1:9; 2:9-10) is not settled by this verse.

decisions.choice: robes made white in blood: cleansed by the Lamb's death
decisions.reason: Blood stains, but the Lamb's blood makes clean. Their robes are white because the Lamb's death has freed them from their sins (1:5) and they have trusted in it. Israel washed their clothes to be ready to meet God (Exodus 19:10, 14).

decisions.choice: the elder's words continue to 7:17
decisions.reason: The answer goes on through 7:17 as one speech, so the quotation stays open.

decisions.choice: affliction (L, B); terrible suffering (R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:9, "affliction" renders θλίψεως. The phrase is widely known as "the great tribulation".

source.text: διὰ τοῦτό εἰσιν ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ λατρεύουσιν αὐτῷ ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτὸς ἐν τῷ ναῷ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ἐπὶ τοῦ θρόνου σκηνώσει ἐπ’ αὐτούς.

records.literal_gloss: Because of this they are before the throne of the God, and they serve him day and night in the temple of him, and the [one] sitting on the throne will tent over them.

en.L: Therefore they are before the throne of God, and they serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} day and night in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} temple, and the one seated on the throne will spread {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} tent over them.
en.B: For this reason they stand before God's throne and serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} day and night in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} temple, and the one who sits on the throne will spread {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} tent over them.
en.R: That is why they stand in front of God's throne. They serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} day and night in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} temple. And the one who sits on the throne will live among them and protect them.

decisions.choice: serve: worship as priests
decisions.reason: λατρεύουσιν is the word for the service of worship, especially the work of priests in the temple. They are the kingdom of priests of 1:6 and 5:10.

decisions.choice: God will tent over them: his presence, as in the tabernacle
decisions.reason: σκηνώσει comes from the word for a tent. God lived among Israel in the tabernacle (Exodus 40:34-38), and Ezekiel 37:27 promises, "My dwelling place shall be with them." John 1:14 uses the same verb of the Word who "pitched his tent among us", and Revelation 21:3 announces that God's dwelling is with people.

decisions.choice: spread his tent over them (L, B); live among them and protect them (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the picture of the tent; Readable says what it means (m2).

source.text: οὐ πεινάσουσιν ἔτι οὐδὲ διψήσουσιν ἔτι, οὐδὲ μὴ πέσῃ ἐπ’ αὐτοὺς ὁ ἥλιος οὐδὲ πᾶν καῦμα, ὅτι τὸ ἀρνίον τὸ ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ θρόνου ποιμανεῖ αὐτούς, καὶ ὁδηγήσει αὐτοὺς ἐπὶ ζωῆς πηγὰς ὑδάτων· καὶ ἐξαλείψει ὁ θεὸς πᾶν δάκρυον ἐκ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Not they will hunger anymore nor will thirst anymore, nor not will fall on them the sun nor any scorching heat, \v 17 because the Lamb the [one] in middle of the throne will shepherd them and will lead them to of life springs of waters, and will wipe out the God every tear out of the eyes of them.

en.L: They will not hunger anymore, nor thirst anymore, nor will the sun strike them, nor any scorching heat, \v 17 because the Lamb who is in the middle of the throne will shepherd them and will guide them to springs of the waters of life, and God will wipe away every tear from their eyes."
en.B: No more will they go hungry, no more will they be thirsty; the sun will not strike them, nor any burning heat. \v 17 For the Lamb in the midst of the throne will shepherd them and guide them to springs of the water of life, and every tear God will wipe from their eyes."
en.R: They will never be hungry or thirsty again. The sun and the hot wind will never burn them. \v 17 The Lamb at the center of the throne will take care of them like a shepherd. He will lead them to springs of water that give life. And God will wipe away all their tears."

decisions.choice: Isaiah 49:10: no hunger, thirst or heat, and springs of water
decisions.reason: Isaiah 49:10 promises the returning exiles: "They shall not hunger or thirst, neither scorching wind nor sun shall strike them, for he who has pity on them will lead them, and by springs of water will guide them." Psalm 23 gives the picture of the shepherd who leads to water.

decisions.choice: God will wipe away every tear: Isaiah 25:8
decisions.reason: Isaiah 25:8 says that God will swallow up death forever and wipe away tears from all faces. Revelation 21:4 repeats the promise.

decisions.choice: the Lamb is the shepherd
decisions.reason: The Lamb who was slaughtered becomes the shepherd of the flock, the role God takes in Ezekiel 34:23 and Psalm 23. ποιμανεῖ is the verb of 2:27, there used of ruling with an iron rod; here it is the care of a shepherd.

decisions.choice: springs of the water of life: "life" stands first
decisions.reason: The Greek puts "of life" first for emphasis: the springs give life (compare 21:6; 22:1, 17).
